parts.text: In this experiment, you will determine the mass of an object using two strings. The apparatus has been set up for you. Do not change the position of the rule or the distance between the stands. You are also provided with two loops of string labelled P and Q . Carry out the following instructions, referring to Figs. 1.1 and 1.2. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: i
parts.text: (a) (i) Record the scale reading a 0 on the rule, at point A, where the string crosses the rule, as indicated in Fig. 1.1. a 0 = ...............................................................

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) Carefully place loop P around the vertical strings so that the strings are pulled closer together as shown in Fig. 1.2. The loop must be horizontal and should be just above the rule. Fig. 1.2

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Record in Table 1.1 the scale reading a 1 at point A 1 , as indicated in Fig. 1.2.

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Record in Table 1.1 the scale reading b 1 at point B 1 . Table 1.1 loop a 1 / cm b 1 / cm d A / cm d B / cm M / g P Q

parts.label: iii
parts.text: (iii) Calculate and record in the table the distance d A , as indicated in Fig. 1.2. Use your results from (a)(i) and from the table. d A is the difference between a 0 and a 1 .

parts.label: iv
parts.text: (iv) Calculate and record the distance d B . Use your results from (a)(ii) and from the table. d B is the difference between b 0 and b 1 .

parts.label: v
parts.text: (v) Calculate and record in the table a value for the mass M of object X , using your results from the table and the equation M = k d B d A , where k = 100 g.

parts.label: vi
parts.text: (vi) Remove loop P from the vertical strings and replace it with loop Q .

parts.label: vii
parts.text: (vii) Repeat steps (b)(i) to (b)(v) for loop Q . [5]
